feed.title: Quantum Computing — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: QPlayLearn
entry.summary: An education project explaining quantum concepts at three separate depths: game, animation and technical account. Unlike single-level resources that layering lets the same concept reach a child and an undergraduate.

entry.title: Quantum Flytrap
entry.summary: A virtual lab where you assemble and run optical quantum experiments by dragging photons, polarisers and beam splitters. Unlike circuit simulators it works at the level of the physical apparatus rather than the qubit abstraction.

entry.title: Virtual Quantum Optics Laboratory
entry.summary: A browser-based laboratory for designing and simulating quantum optics experiments. Against Quantum Flytrap it aims at research-grade accuracy rather than gamification, enough to stand in for a teaching lab.

entry.title: TensorFlow Quantum
entry.summary: Wraps parameterised quantum circuits as Keras-style layers to combine with classical networks — where hybrid classical-quantum models get explored experimentally.

entry.title: IBM Quantum
entry.summary: Queued access to real quantum processors, with circuits written and submitted through Qiskit. The noise and error rates a simulator hides only show up here.

entry.title: Neden Q#?
entry.summary: Explains why quantum needs its own language — no-cloning and measurement collapsing state do not fit classical language idioms.

entry.title: LIQUi|>
entry.summary: Microsoft’s early quantum simulation platform, since superseded by Q#. Little practical value now beyond seeing how the field’s toolchain evolved.

entry.title: Q# Geliştirme Kiti Kurulumu
entry.summary: Installing Q# and the QDK, with the VS Code extension as the shortest path to running circuits on a local simulator — no hardware access needed to start.

entry.title: Microsoft QDK
entry.summary: Source for the Q# compiler and simulator — for anyone who wants to see how a quantum circuit is compiled and simulated.

entry.title: Microsoft Kuantum Yol Haritası
entry.summary: The stages from noisy intermediate-scale (NISQ) to error-corrected logical qubits — useful for weighing which of the field’s promises are now and which are a decade out.

entry.title: Kuantum Öğrenme Kaynakları
entry.summary: A Turkish compilation of quantum computing learning resources — an ordered way into the field.
